summary: Petition under Section 79(1)(c) and (k) of the Electricity Act, 2003 read with Regulation 41 and 42 of the Central Electricity Regulatory Commission (Connectivity and General Network Access to the interstate Transmission System) Regulations, 2022 inter alia seeking relaxation from submission of Conn-BG2 in terms of Regulation 37.10(b) read with Regulation 8.2(a). Hyderabad - 500032, Telangana, India. . . **Petitioner No. 1** Hyderabad - 500032, Telangana, India. .. . **Petitioner No. 2** Hyderabad - 500032, Telangana, India. . . **Petitioner No. 3** Order in Petition No. 21/MP/2026 Order in Petition No. 21/MP/2026 - _g) Pass such other or further order(s) as this Hon’ble Commission may deem fit and proper in the facts and circumstances of the present case._ - _a) Grant ad-interim ex-parte relief to the Petitioners restraining CTUIL from taking any coercive action against the Petitioners with respect to the connectivity applications bearing nos. 2200001655, 2200001712 and 2200001734 dated 15.01.2025, 29.01.2025, and 03.02.2025 made by EG Clean, EG Pavan and EG Solaire, respectively, during pendency of the present Petition; and/or_ - _b) Pass such other or further order(s) as this Hon’ble Commission may deem fit and proper in the facts and circumstances of the present case._ Order in Petition No. 21/MP/2026 Order in Petition No. 21/MP/2026 Order in Petition No. 21/MP/2026 **4.** During the hearing, the Petition was admitted and CTUIL was directed to file its reply along with clarification on the in-principle grant issued to EG Pavan, wherein 220kV bay is proposed at Sec-II of the JK-II PS while connectivity granted at Kalyanpur PS. Order in Petition No. 21/MP/2026 - e) At the stage of issuing in-principle approvals to EG Pavan and EG Solaire, Conn-BG2 was recorded as “NIL”. This notation was made on the basis of the Order in Petition No. 21/MP/2026 Order in Petition No. 21/MP/2026 Order in Petition No. 21/MP/2026 - n) The Petitioners furnished Conn-BGs to CTUIL only by letters dated 30.09.2025, and thereafter amended the same on 13.10.2025 on account of discrepancies such as change of address and company name. This unequivocally demonstrates that, as on the effective date of the Third Amendment (09.09.2025), the Petitioners’ cases had not attained finality, rather connectivity process was at the in-principle stage. Order in Petition No. 21/MP/2026 **6.** The Petitioners, vide its rejoinder dated 10.02.2026, have submitted as under: - a) The Petitioner submitted Conn-BG1 and Conn-BG3 to CTUIL and EG Clean furnished Conn-BG2 in terms of the in-principle approval, whereas the inprinciple approvals granted to EG Pavan and EG Solaire recorded Conn-BG2 as “NIL” and therefore, EG Pavan and EG Solaire were not required to submit Conn-BG2. Order in Petition No. 21/MP/2026 Order in Petition No. 21/MP/2026 **7.** During the hearing dated 24.02.2026, learned counsel(s) of Petitioner(s) and Respondent argued at length and concluded their arguments, considering this Commission reserved matter for Order. As per the above, the Petitioner(s) deposited the required Conn BGs within timeline Order in Petition No. 21/MP/2026 Order in Petition No. 21/MP/2026 **13.** We have perused submissions of the Petitioner(s), Respondent and perused information Order in Petition No. 21/MP/2026 Order in Petition No. 21/MP/2026 Order in Petition No. 21/MP/2026 Order in Petition No. 21/MP/2026 Order in Petition No. 21/MP/2026 **22.** It is also worth mentioning that no substantive rights of Petitioner No. 2 and Petitioner No. 3 are affected by CTUIL’s notice dated 05.12.2025 in as much as the Connectivity stands secured. The procedural compliances as necessary and as stipulated in the Regulations have been insisted by CTUIL, wherein this Commission does not feel any necessity of interference. Order in Petition No. 21/MP/2026 Order in Petition No. 21/MP/2026
